# Regula

> Open-source CLI reporting code-observable AI-governance indicators across 3 jurisdiction reference sets. It maps findings to 13 framework references for contextual human review; it does not determine legal classification or compliance. The core install has no required third-party runtime dependencies. Optional features may add dependencies or network access. Install: `pipx install regula-ai`.
> **Not affiliated with Regula Forensics** (regula.com, identity verification). This is Regula the AI governance CLI at getregula.com.

Regula combines two approaches: (1) static code analysis for risk patterns, dependency security, credential exposure, and bias indicators, and (2) questionnaire-based assessment for organisational obligations code cannot verify (Articles 9, 17, 27, 72). Multi-jurisdiction: use `--jurisdictions eu,korea,colorado` to map findings to all three regulatory frameworks simultaneously. It explicitly documents what it cannot do -- see docs/what-regula-does-not-do.md.

## FAQ

- **What is Regula?** An open-source CLI that reports code-observable AI-governance indicators across 3 jurisdiction reference sets. It supports 8 language families at unequal analysis depth, maps findings to 13 framework references, and generates reviewer-completable evidence scaffolds. It does not determine legal classification or compliance. The core install has no required third-party runtime dependencies; optional features may add dependencies or network access.
- **What jurisdictions does Regula cover?** EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689), South Korea AI Basic Act (Act No. 20676, in force 22 Jan 2026), and Colorado SB 26-189 (disclosure-focused with consumer correction and human-review rights, duties from 1 Jan 2027). Use `--jurisdictions eu,korea,colorado` on `regula check` or select a jurisdiction at https://getregula.com/assess/. Each jurisdiction has its own domain-to-obligation mapping.
- **What does Regula NOT do?** It does not determine final legal risk classification (that depends on intended purpose and deployment context, which are business decisions). It does not verify organisational compliance processes (Articles 9, 17, 27, 72). It does not replace legal advice. See [what-regula-does-not-do.md](https://github.com/kuzivaai/getregula/blob/main/docs/what-regula-does-not-do.md) for the full scope statement.
- **What frameworks does Regula map to?** EU AI Act, ISO 42001, NIST AI RMF, NIST CSF, SOC 2, ISO 27001, OWASP LLM Top 10, OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, MITRE ATLAS, ICO/DSIT UK AI principles, LGPD, Brazil's Marco Legal da IA, and the EU Cyber Resilience Act (13 frameworks total via `references/framework_crosswalk.yaml`). South Korea AI Basic Act and Colorado SB 26-189 coverage is separate, via the jurisdiction layer (`--jurisdictions korea,colorado`; `kr` and `co` are accepted aliases).
- **When are the EU AI Act application dates?** The original Article 5 prohibitions have applied since 2 Feb 2025. GPAI obligations began applying on 2 Aug 2025, subject to transition rules. Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 sets 2 Dec 2027 for Annex III high-risk provisions and 2 Aug 2028 for the Annex I product path. Article 50 generally has applied since 2 Aug 2026; providers of Article 50(2) systems already on the market before then have until 2 Dec 2026. Confirm role, scope, and transitions in the enacted text.
- **Does the EU AI Act apply outside the EU?** Yes. Article 2(1)(c) applies extraterritorially to any provider or deployer whose AI system output is used within the EU, regardless of where the company is established.
- **How accurate is Regula?** Published precision on a random corpus of 115 real-world findings (N=115): 83.5%, measured on v1.7.0 and labelled by a single reviewer with no inter-rater agreement measurement. See [benchmarks](https://github.com/kuzivaai/getregula/blob/main/docs/benchmarks/PRECISION_RECALL_2026_04.md) for methodology and confidence intervals.
